bug_semantics: The standard HR employee-create form collected an email and employee details but no password, while EmployeeSaveController::save() assigned bcrypt($request->input('password', 'changeme')). Consequently, every employee created through that product flow received the same predictable literal credential. The created record was App\Models\User, an Illuminate Authenticatable model used by the normal login path, so a remote attacker who knew an onboarded employee's email could log in as that employee with changeme; no first-login change or reset step invalidated the credential.
flaw_origin: The smallest first-writer is decomposed pull-request member 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6. It created EmployeeSaveController with the changeme fallback, created the shared passwordless employee form, registered POST /rrhh/employee/save, and advanced APP_VERSION from 5.9.2 to 5.10.0. GitHub squash 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64 aggregated that member and 8369823e08d5ce346527ae6950a588619f821bc6; the latter changed only routes/module/payroll.php, so the aggregate is not the smallest BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the complete commit object for BIC 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 names human author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com> and its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/marker
evidence: First-party Secur0 advisory https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-19871-hardcoded-credentials-in-prospero-flow-crm-employee-onboarding identifies EmployeeSaveController, the passwordless shared form, affected versions beginning with the module at 5.10.0 and before 5.15.9, vulnerable tag v5.14.0, and advisory fix https://github.com/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/commit/5cc01ed958db4ad0a026a8daa1c6a8bb98a43e66. `git log -L '/validated.*password/,+1':app/Http/Controllers/Rrhh/Employee/EmployeeSaveController.php 5cc01ed9...` traces the exact line from its creation as `$validated['password'] = bcrypt($request->input('password', 'changeme'));` in mainline squash 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64 to replacement by `bcrypt(Str::random(32))` in 5cc01ed958db4ad0a026a8daa1c6a8bb98a43e66; `git log --all -S"'changeme'" -- <controller>` returns only those introduction/removal mainline commits. GitHub API `GET /repos/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/pulls/258/commits` reconstructs members 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 (parent 9e4f84ece7e13c2c327540804dcaf841c6ac23fa) and 8369823e08d5ce346527ae6950a588619f821bc6; `git show 33a30a5d...` proves the first member created the controller, passwordless `_form.blade.php`, RRHH route, and version 5.10.0, while `git show 8369823e...` proves the second touched only the payroll update route. The final member tree a74da6513163046124c133789294353d268087bd equals squash 04d1afd7's tree, proving incorporation. Direct parent verification with `git ls-tree -r --name-only 9e4f84ece7e13c2c327540804dcaf841c6ac23fa -- app/Http/Controllers/Rrhh/Employee/EmployeeSaveController.php resources/views/rrhh/employee/_form.blade.php routes/module/rrhh.php` produced no paths: the controller, form, route, and vulnerable assignment were absent. At the BIC, `app/Models/User.php` extends Illuminate's Authenticatable and accepts password in `$fillable`; the form contains no password input. MainController has auth middleware for the staff onboarding operation, but the resulting employee User credential is usable by an otherwise unauthenticated attacker at the normal login. Version checks: the BIC changes version.php from 5.9.2 to 5.10.0; `git tag --contains 04d1afd7...` returns v5.14.0 and `git show v5.14.0:version.php` says 5.14.0, while that tag still has changeme. `git show 5cc01ed9...:version.php` says 5.15.9 and `git tag --contains 5cc01ed9...` returns no tag, matching the advisory's statement that the fix is not yet tagged. `git show c58853a4e3d4cdb554955363a8d0ea8946c869e8 -- <controller>` shows the first direct PR #263 member removing changeme for a random temporary password; the final squash further uses a 32-byte random password, sets must_change_password, assigns the User role, and sends a password-reset link. GitHub PR #263 commit API links c58853a4e3d4cdb554955363a8d0ea8946c869e8 to the fix series, and the final PR-member tree 9e51bc96e7e3cab0302b773b88fa32529a84042c equals the 5cc01ed9 squash tree. Finally, `git cat-file -p 33a30a5d...` is the BIC-only AI check: human author/committer Gustavo Novaro and no trailers or AI marker.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle begins atomically in PR #258's first member: the controller hard-codes a default credential at the same time the only standard onboarding form omits a password and the route/model make a real login-capable User. Its immediate parent has none of those HR files, so this is creation rather than a move or refactor. The public mainline squash is one commit later only in representation: the PR API preserves the two member objects, the first member contains every causal line, the second is an unrelated payroll-route correction, and the aggregate tree matches the final member tree. Thus 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 is smaller than 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64 and is the real BIC. The module entered at 5.10.0, remained present in tagged 5.14.0, and was removed at the repository's 5.15.9 commit. Fix member c58853a4e3d4cdb554955363a8d0ea8946c869e8 first eliminates the shared literal; advisory fix squash 5cc01ed958db4ad0a026a8daa1c6a8bb98a43e66 lands the final random-password/reset-link/forced-change design. Attribution is judged only from the decomposed BIC commit object, not the squash, PR text, or fix: it contains a human author and committer and no AI marker. Therefore the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
